solution_overview:
A hospital tracked 30-day readmissions across three discharge units. We are given the number of patients discharged from each unit and the number of those patients who were readmitted within 30 days. One discharge record is pulled at random.

Let $R$ be the event that a patient is readmitted within 30 days. Let $D_{\text{ICU}}$, $D_{\text{GW}}$, and $D_{\text{OP}}$ be the events that a patient was discharged from the ICU, General Ward, or Outpatient unit, respectively. The given counts define the sample space of 24,000 patient records:

ICU: $N_{\text{ICU}} = 4\text{,}000$ total, $N_{R \cap D_{\text{ICU}}} = 640$ readmitted.
General Ward: $N_{\text{GW}} = 12\text{,}000$ total, $N_{R \cap D_{\text{GW}}} = 960$ readmitted.
Outpatient: $N_{\text{OP}} = 8\text{,}000$ total, $N_{R \cap D_{\text{OP}}} = 240$ readmitted.

Total number of discharged patients: $N_{\text{Total}} = N_{\text{ICU}} + N_{\text{GW}} + N_{\text{OP}}$.
$$N_{\text{Total}} = 4\text{,}000 + 12\text{,}000 + 8\text{,}000 = 24\text{,}000$$
Total number of readmitted patients: $N_{R} = N_{R \cap D_{\text{ICU}}} + N_{R \cap D_{\text{GW}}} + N_{R \cap D_{\text{OP}}}$.
$$N_{R} = 640 + 960 + 240 = 1\text{,}840$$
Total number of non-readmitted patients: $N_{R^c} = N_{\text{Total}} - N_{R}$.
$$N_{R^c} = 24\text{,}000 - 1\text{,}840 = 22\text{,}160$$

Probabilities are calculated as ratios of counts from these totals.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

The probability that a randomly selected patient was readmitted is the ratio of the total number of readmitted patients to the total number of discharged patients.

$$P(R) = \frac{N_R}{N_{\text{Total}}}$$

$$P(R) = \frac{1\text{,}840}{24\text{,}000}$$

$$P(R) \approx 0.07667$$

$$P(R) \approx 7.67\%$$

Since $7.67\% \not> 8\%$, the statement is False.

**B.** → False

The probability that a patient is readmitted given they were discharged from the ICU is the conditional probability $P(R \mid D_{\text{ICU}})$. This is the ratio of readmitted ICU patients to the total ICU patients.

$$P(R \mid D_{\text{ICU}}) = \frac{N_{R \cap D_{\text{ICU}}}}{N_{\text{ICU}}}$$

$$P(R \mid D_{\text{ICU}}) = \frac{640}{4\text{,}000}$$

$$P(R \mid D_{\text{ICU}}) = 0.16$$

$$P(R \mid D_{\text{ICU}}) = 16\%$$

Since $16\% \not> 17\%$, the statement is False.

**C.** → False

The probability that a readmitted patient was discharged from the General Ward is the conditional probability $P(D_{\text{GW}} \mid R)$. This is the ratio of readmitted General Ward patients to the total number of readmitted patients.

$$P(D_{\text{GW}} \mid R) = \frac{N_{R \cap D_{\text{GW}}}}{N_R}$$

$$P(D_{\text{GW}} \mid R) = \frac{960}{1\text{,}840}$$

$$P(D_{\text{GW}} \mid R) \approx 0.5217$$

$$P(D_{\text{GW}} \mid R) \approx 52.17\%$$

Since $52.17\% \not> 53\%$, the statement is False.

**D.** → False

The probability that a readmitted patient was discharged from the ICU or Outpatient unit is $P(D_{\text{ICU}} \cup D_{\text{OP}} \mid R)$. Since these two discharge units are mutually exclusive, this is $P(D_{\text{ICU}} \mid R) + P(D_{\text{OP}} \mid R)$. This is also the ratio of the combined number of readmitted ICU and Outpatient patients to the total number of readmitted patients.

$$P(D_{\text{ICU}} \cup D_{\text{OP}} \mid R) = \frac{N_{R \cap D_{\text{ICU}}} + N_{R \cap D_{\text{OP}}}}{N_R}$$

$$P(D_{\text{ICU}} \cup D_{\text{OP}} \mid R) = \frac{640 + 240}{1\text{,}840}$$

$$P(D_{\text{ICU}} \cup D_{\text{OP}} \mid R) = \frac{880}{1\text{,}840}$$

$$P(D_{\text{ICU}} \cup D_{\text{OP}} \mid R) \approx 0.4783$$

$$P(D_{\text{ICU}} \cup D_{\text{OP}} \mid R) \approx 47.83\%$$

Since $47.83\% \not> 49\%$, the statement is False.

**E.** → True

The probability that a patient was not readmitted, $P(R^c)$, is the complement of the probability that a patient was readmitted, $P(R)$.

$$P(R^c) = 1 - P(R)$$

Using the value from **A.**:

$$P(R^c) = 1 - 0.07666...$$

$$P(R^c) \approx 0.92333$$

$$P(R^c) \approx 92.33\%$$

Since $92.33\% > 92\%$, the statement is True.
